title: Throughput guardrails and sizing autopilot for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: deliver a production-ready feature set that enforces throughput SLOs for Dedicated capacity while recommending and optionally applying per-pool size adjustments to minimize cost without violating latency SLAs. This ticket covers three coordinated capabilities: (1) Throughput Guardrails: policy-driven hard/soft throughput floors and ceilings per tenant/fleet with automatic fallback, (2) Sizing Autopilot: a predictive sizing engine that suggests pool commit adjustments and optional auto-apply windows, and (3) Utilization Reporting: new per-pool telemetry surfaced in Console and via API that shows utilization histograms, tail latency by model/sequence length, and heatmaps for burst patterns. Unlike earlier advisor work, this effort focuses on continuous closed-loop actions (suggest -> validate on a shadow run -> optionally apply) and safe rollouts with canary enforcement and automatic rollback on SLA regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Admins can set throughput guardrails (min qps, max qps, enforcement mode: warn/enforce) per dedicated pool via API and Console.
2) Sizing Autopilot produces time-series-backed recommendations with expected cost delta and risk score for each pool and a suggested commit (GPUs/slots).
3) Console shows utilization histogram, 95th/99th token latency breakdown, and burst heatmap for selected intervals (last 7/30/90 days).
4) An opt-in 'autopilot' mode can apply sizing changes during a maintenance window and will run a 1-hour shadow validation before committing; rollback triggers if latency SLA degrades beyond threshold.
5) Feature includes unit/integration tests, a migration plan for existing pools, and docs + runbook for SREs.
6) Telemetry adds new metrics (pool_qps_limit, pool_qps_actual, pool_commit_recommendation, sizing_risk_score) and events for guardrail violations.
implementation_plan: Phase A (2 sprints): schema and telemetry: add new metrics to daemon, extend pool config proto with guardrail fields, ingest new series into TSDB. Phase B (2 sprints): sizing autopilot MVP: offline trainer that consumes 90 days of traces, generates recommendations and explainability fields, UI for review-only suggestions. Phase C (2 sprints): safe apply path: shadow validation, canary rollout, automatic rollback, and console controls for enforcement mode. Phase D (1 sprint): documentation, runbook, performance testing, and GA release. Rollout strategy: start with internal teams -> beta customers (voluntary) -> opt-out for high-risk pools -> GA. Backwards compatibility: default guardrail mode = warn, autopilot disabled by default.

risk_and_mitigation: Risks: (1) Autopilot could reduce committed capacity too aggressively and cause SLA violations; mitigation: conservative scoring, shadow validation, and require two successful runs before auto-apply. (2) Telemetry skew could give noisy recommendations; mitigation: 90-day smoothing window + percentile bucketing and minimum sample threshold. (3) Edge-case models with bursty short sequences may appear underutilized; mitigation: burst heatmap and sequence-length-aware simulation in trainer.
metrics_kpis:
- Fleet cost delta (expected vs. baseline) as percentage string
- Number of guardrail violations per week
- % of autopilot recommendations accepted (manual + auto-applied)
- Post-change SLA regression rate (fraction of pools with >5% 99th latency increase)
- Mean time to rollback (minutes)
